decisions.statement: A module is loaded by name through an import made here and named nowhere else.
A module is loaded by awaiting it, so a module the loader serves is reached.
The name a module is loaded by is the name that module is imported by.
The checks are reached only to judge.
A change judged in a scratch tree is judged by the checks at this code's own root.
This file's own location is what the import made here resolves a name against.
A module answering to less than a gate is built from is refused by name.
A gate that will not build is handed back as broken rather than thrown.
The broken answer handed back says only why the gate is missing.
The caller says the meaning of a missing gate.
A gate nobody could build judges nothing rather than passing everything.
The gate is built for one phase.
The phase a gate is built for is the caller's, and a caller naming none means the change.
Which checks sit on a phase is answered where the checks are.
Nothing here judges.
Nothing here writes.
Nothing here indexes.
Nothing here commits.
No root is worked out here.
The gate handed back is the gate that will judge.
This module is never told whether the gate ran.
`loadedBy` names a page type, and this loads two modules by name, so nothing declares it.
The checks a change alters are loaded as that change leaves those checks.

definition: the checks and the index loaded by name when wanted, and the gate built from them
